evals.prompt: Create a Storybook story file for a Button component. The button has a size prop (sm, md, lg), a variant prop (primary, ghost), and a disabled state. Set up the controls with categories, sensible defaults, and three named stories.
evals.expected_output: Default export with argTypes using table.category grouping, args with sensible defaults including size: 'md', and three named stories using Template.bind({}) — no component name repeated in story names.
expectations: Default export includes title, component, argTypes, and args
size control uses options ['sm', 'md', 'lg'] — not spelled-out values like 'small', 'medium', 'large'
Default args include size: 'md' (not 'medium' or 'default')
size and variant controls are categorized with table: { category: 'Variant' }
disabled/isDisabled control is categorized with table: { category: 'State' }
All named stories use the Template.bind({}) pattern
Story names do not repeat the component name (e.g. 'Default' not 'Button Default')
No 'default' or 'normal' appears as a control option value

evals.prompt: Create a template.js file for a Card component. The card has a title, optional body text, an optional image at the top, and a featured modifier that adds a highlighted border. Follow the standard template patterns.
evals.expected_output: Exports a named Template function using lit html. Accepts rootClass, customClasses, customStyles, id, testId as standard args alongside card-specific props. Uses classMap for the featured modifier and ifDefined for optional attributes. Image is only rendered when provided.
expectations: Exports a named Template function
Accepts rootClass, id, testId, customClasses, customStyles as standard arguments
Uses classMap to conditionally apply the featured modifier class based on rootClass
Uses ifDefined for optional attributes such as id and data-testid
Does not hardcode BEM class names — derives modifier classes dynamically from rootClass
Image is rendered conditionally — only when an image prop is provided

evals.prompt: Set up a visual regression test file for Chromatic for a Button component.
evals.expected_output: A component.test.js that imports Template from ./template.js, enables Chromatic snapshots, hides stories from the sidebar with tags, and groups multiple button states into a single grid rather than one story per variant.
expectations: Imports Template from ./template.js
Sets chromatic: { disableSnapshot: false } in parameters
VRT stories are tagged with ['!autodocs', '!dev'] to hide them from the sidebar
Does not duplicate button markup — calls Template directly
Groups multiple states or variants into a single snapshot story rather than a separate story per state

evals.prompt: Write the template.js for a Dropdown component. It renders a Button as its trigger and a panel as its content. Clicking the trigger should toggle the dropdown open/closed.
evals.expected_output: Imports Button Template via a path alias (not a relative path). Calls the Button Template for the trigger. Uses context.updateArgs to toggle isOpen on click. Does not copy button HTML markup.
expectations: Imports Button Template from a path alias like @design-system/button/stories/template.js — not a relative path
Calls the imported Button Template function rather than duplicating button HTML markup
Uses context.updateArgs to toggle isOpen state when the trigger is clicked
Passes passthroughs into the Button Template call so Button's own args still work
The trigger is defined as a callback function, not inline HTML

evals.prompt: I have a basic story file for a Tag component with just a Default story. Add stories for: a removable variant (showRemove: true), a disabled state, and small and large size variants.
evals.expected_output: Four new named stories added using Template.bind({}), each with only the args needed to demonstrate the specific variant. Names are concise and don't repeat 'Tag'. The existing Default story and default export are untouched.
expectations: Four new named stories are added using Template.bind({})
Each story sets only the args that distinguish it from the default — not a full copy of all default args
Story names are concise and do not include the word 'Tag' (e.g. 'Removable' not 'TagRemovable')
The existing Default story and default export are unchanged
No new Template function is defined — the imported Template is used directly
